evidence: M-O s.v. pleated, ruffled: Vives, collāre rūgātum, a pleated collar
Plin. NH 9.102: testae rūgātae, ridged shells (Lewis & Short s.v. rūgō)
terms.comment: The participle of rūgō, crease: Plautus says of a cloak vidē palliolum ut rūgat, see how it creases (Cas. 2.3.30, Lewis & Short), and the folds of a garment are rūgae (Plin. NH 35.56, Lewis & Short s.v. rūga). We have found no classical instance of rūgātus of a garment; Vives uses it so.

evidence: Varr. ap. Non. 189.26: togae undulātae (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Traupman’s word for pleated, but Lewis & Short has only “diversified as with waves, like watered stuffs”: Varro’s togae undulātae had a wavy pattern, not folds.

sources: Lewis & Short: rugo · Lewis & Short: ruga
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.vv. pleated, ruffled; pleat, ruffle.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 117.
